statements.status_notes: CVE-2022-0839 is an XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability in Liquibase Core versions prior to 4.8.0 via the SAXParser. An attacker could exploit this to read arbitrary files or perform server-side request forgery (SSRF) through crafted XML changelog files.
statements.impact_statement: XXE vulnerability fixed in Liquibase 4.8.0. Our liquibase-core is built from source with the fix included. Scanner incorrectly matches the non-semantic version format (master-<sha>).

GraalVM Python setuptools ReDoS vulnerability. setuptools is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its package management functions are never invoked at runtime. This CVE requires setuptools to parse HTML during package lookup; no package lookups occur since all packages are pre-installed at build time via Maven graalpy-maven-plugin.

Stack exhaustion DoS in json-smart via unlimited recursive parsing of deeply nested JSON arrays and objects. Requires parsing attacker-controlled untrusted JSON input. Liquibase is a CLI tool that only processes JSON from local operator-controlled configuration files and database metadata. No network-facing JSON parsing surface exists.
Fixed in azure-identity 1.10.0. Liquibase Secure uses azure-identity 1.18.2, which includes the fix.

urllib3 cookie header leak vulnerability. urllib3 is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its HTTP client functionality is never invoked at runtime. No HTTP requests are made via Python at runtime.

statements.status_notes: A timing-based side-channel flaw was found in libgcrypt's RSA implementation that may allow a remote attacker to initiate a Bleichenbacher-style attack, which can lead to the decryption of RSA ciphertexts.
statements.impact_statement: A timing side-channel in libgcrypt's RSA implementation could enable a Bleichenbacher-style decryption attack (the "Marvin Attack"). The container base image currently ships libgcrypt20 1.10.3-2ubuntu0.2, the fixed release (confirmed by pulling the current base image and checking installed package versions directly, since this OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the base image resolves to at build time). Independent of the version, checking the Java runtime's own library linkage shows it does not link libgcrypt at all; the package is pulled in only as a dependency of GnuPG/apt/systemd tooling (gpg, gpgv, gpg-agent, dirmngr, libapt-pkg, libsystemd0), none of which Liquibase invokes. Java uses its own JCE crypto providers, not system libgcrypt.
Fixed in azure-identity 1.12.2. Liquibase Secure uses azure-identity 1.18.2, which includes the fix.
Fixed in msal4j 1.15.1. Liquibase Secure uses msal4j 1.23.1, which includes the fix.

sqlparse ReDoS vulnerability. sqlparse is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its SQL parsing functionality is never invoked at runtime. Liquibase uses its own Java SQL parser; the Python sqlparse module is never called.
False CPE match. cassandra-driver-kerberos is not the Authenticator 2FA app. The vulnerability applies to the Authenticator mobile application.

statements.status_notes: Denial-of-service on Windows applications using Netty. Netty attempts to read OS identification files even on Windows systems where they don't natively exist. An attacker with local access can create an oversized (>1GB) file at these paths, causing Netty to load it into memory and exhaust the JVM heap, crashing the application.
statements.impact_statement: Netty's PlatformDependent unconditionally attempts to read /etc/os-release and /usr/lib/os-release-style paths for OS identification, including on Windows where these paths don't natively exist. Exploitation requires an attacker who already has local filesystem write access sufficient to plant a >1GB file at one of these root-level paths ahead of JVM startup — a precondition that itself requires the host to already be compromised at a level exceeding what this DoS provides. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver; Liquibase does not read or configure these paths itself.

statements.status_notes: Git, before versions 2.48.1, 2.47.3, 2.46.5, 2.45.4, and 2.44.3, has a vulnerability where a Git client using a terminal that supports ANSI escape sequences can have those sequences, when written to the sideband channel used by the server to transmit informational or error messages during clone/fetch/push, misrepresent the state of a fetch/pull/push or otherwise mislead the user into executing untrusted scripts.
statements.impact_statement: Exploitation requires cloning, fetching from, or pushing to an attacker-controlled Git remote that injects malicious ANSI escape sequences over the sideband channel. Liquibase runtime code never shells out to `git clone`, `git fetch`, or `git push` against any remote — a stronger, structural argument than merely trusting a given remote. A source review confirmed no process/exec invocation of git anywhere in Liquibase's runtime code. The only git usage in this repo at all is CI's own checkout step, which clones this repository's own trusted GitHub remote with a git binary version pinned by the runner image, not by this repo — not the exploit scenario this CVE describes.

Stack exhaustion DoS in json-smart via deeply nested JSON with many { characters (incomplete fix for CVE-2023-1370). Requires parsing attacker-controlled untrusted JSON input. Liquibase is a CLI tool that only processes JSON from local operator-controlled configuration files and database metadata. No network-facing JSON parsing surface exists.

GraalVM Python setuptools command injection vulnerability. setuptools is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its package management functions are never invoked at runtime. This CVE requires setuptools to process URLs via download/install functions; those functions are never called at runtime.

statements.status_notes:
Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm vulnerability in Legion of the Bouncy Castle Inc. BC-JAVA bcprov on all (core modules).
This vulnerability is associated with program files G3413CTRBlockCipher.
This issue affects BC-JAVA: from 1.59 before 1.80.2, from 1.81 before 1.81.1, from 1.82 before 1.84.
statements.impact_statement:
Remediated. This affected bcprov-jdk18on from 1.59 before 1.80.2, from 1.81 before 1.81.1, and from 1.82 before 1.84; Liquibase Secure now ships org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.85 via the managed bouncycastle.version pin in the root pom.xml, so the vulnerable code is not present in the distribution. The prior code-not-reachable analysis is retained below for the versions that shipped 1.78.1. [TECHOPS-1130]
Bouncy Castle BC-JAVA GOST 28147 CTR mode keystream reuse affects bcprov-jdk18on versions from 1.59 before 1.80.2, from 1.81 before 1.81.1, and from 1.82 before 1.84. Liquibase Secure distribution includes org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.78.1 (core/liquibase-dist/src/main/archive/licenses/commercial/README.txt:1298), which is in the affected range. However, the vulnerable code path is not reachable from Liquibase code: focused greps across Java sources for G3413CTRBlockCipher, GOST28147, GOST, G3413, CTRBlockCipher, GOST28147Engine, and GOST28147ParameterSpec returned zero hits.

statements.status_notes: IO::Uncompress::Unzip versions before 2.215 for Perl propagate an uncaught exception when parsing a zip header with a malformed DOS date. The _dosToUnixTime() function calls Time::Local::timelocal() without an eval guard; a header whose date field decodes to an out-of-range month, day, or hour causes the exception to propagate out of the caller, which expects undef plus an error variable instead.
statements.impact_statement: Perl's IO::Uncompress::Unzip propagates an uncaught exception when a zip header's DOS date field decodes to an out-of-range value. The container's entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI directly (a Java process, not a shell script that shells out to Perl), and a source review found no invocation of perl or any Perl module anywhere in Liquibase's build or runtime. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

Spring Boot EndpointRequest.to() creates a security matcher for null/** instead of the actuator endpoint path when the endpoint is disabled. Requires a running Spring Boot web application with Spring Security and actuator endpoint configuration. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context, never runs an HTTP server, never exposes actuator endpoints, and never configures Spring Security.

statements.status_notes: Apache Tomcat RCE via Default Servlet partial PUT — file fragments uploaded to predictable temp paths trigger deserialization of assembled content. Also enables reading security-sensitive files.
statements.impact_statement: Remote code execution and information disclosure via Tomcat Default Servlet partial PUT support. Requires an HTTP PUT request to a running Tomcat servlet container with partial PUT enabled. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts the Tomcat HTTP server, never deploys any servlet, and never opens any network port. The Default Servlet, partial PUT handling, and file session persistence code paths are never activated.

Netty SslHandler resource exhaustion vulnerability via SSLEngine. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious SSL/TLS data to a Netty server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run a TLS server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections.

statements.status_notes: Denial-of-service on Windows applications using Netty via a null-byte-filled file at an OS-identification path, causing an infinite loop during charset decoding instead of the earlier oversized-file crash.
statements.impact_statement: Incomplete fix to CVE-2024-47535 (see above): a null-byte-filled file at the same Windows os-release-style paths causes InputStreamReader / BufferedReader to loop filling the line buffer with replacement characters without hitting a line break. Same precondition as CVE-2024-47535 — requires an attacker who already has local filesystem write access to plant the malicious file before JVM startup. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver; Liquibase does not read or configure these paths itself.

Spring Framework annotation resolution bypass in generic type hierarchies affecting @EnableMethodSecurity. Requires a running Spring application with method-level security annotations on generic type hierarchies. Liquibase is a CLI tool that does not use Spring Security, does not enable @EnableMethodSecurity, and does not start a Spring application context. The spring-core artifact is a transitive dependency.

GraalVM Python setuptools path traversal vulnerability. setuptools is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its package management functions are never invoked at runtime. This CVE requires setuptools to process package inputs; no package installation or processing occurs at runtime.

Denial of service via excessive memory consumption in Tomcat multipart upload processing. Requires sending a crafted multipart/form-data HTTP POST to a running Tomcat instance. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server and never accepts HTTP requests. The multipart parsing code path is completely inactive.

Denial of service via HTTP/2 stream reset memory leak in Tomcat. Requires an HTTP/2 connection to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never enables HTTP/2, and accepts no inbound network connections.

PostgreSQL JDBC driver channel binding bypass. The vulnerability only triggers when the JDBC connection property channelBinding is explicitly set to "require" (default is "prefer"). Liquibase does not configure channelBinding=require in any default configuration. The vulnerable enforcement code path in ConnectionFactoryImpl.doAuthentication() is not reachable under Liquibase's default configuration.

Denial of service via integer overflow in Tomcat multipart upload file size limit validation. Requires sending a crafted multipart HTTP upload to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server and never processes inbound HTTP requests or multipart uploads.

statements.status_notes: The sort utility's begfield() function in GNU Coreutils is vulnerable to a heap buffer under-read that may allow access to memory outside the allocated buffer when a crafted command uses the traditional key format with an out-of-range character position, due to unsafe pointer arithmetic causing integer wraparound.
statements.impact_statement: GNU coreutils' sort utility has a heap buffer under-read reachable only via the traditional key-specification syntax (+POS1[.C1][OPTS]) with an out-of-range character position. The container's build steps and runtime entrypoint use only rm, ln, mkdir, chown, chmod, wget, tar, unzip, and sha256sum — a source review found no invocation of sort anywhere in this repository's Docker build or runtime path. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships coreutils 9.4-3ubuntu6.3, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: JAXP). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u461, 8u461-perf, 11.0.28, 17.0.16, 21.0.8, 25; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.16 and 21.0.8; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.15.
statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE JAXP vulnerability. The advisory fixes Oracle Java SE 21.0.9, while the scanner reported 21.0.8+9-LTS for this image. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2) and runs the CLI through docker/Dockerfile:68, not an Oracle Java SE or GraalVM client runtime. The Oracle client environment required by the advisory is absent in this deployment.

Denial of service via uncontrolled resource consumption in Tomcat HTTP/2 stream management. Requires an HTTP/2 client connecting to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never enables HTTP/2, and never binds a network port.

statements.status_notes: Connect2id Nimbus JOSE + JWT 10.0.x before 10.0.2 and 9.37.x before 9.37.4 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a deeply nested JSON object supplied in a JWT claim set, because of uncontrolled recursion. Fixed in 9.37.4 and 10.0.2.
statements.impact_statement: A scanner flagged com.nimbusds:nimbus-jose-jwt@10.0.1 as reachable through the com.azure:azure-identity dependency chain used by the Azure extension. Resolving the actual dependency tree shows azure-identity 1.18.4 pulls com.microsoft.azure:msal4j 1.23.1, and msal4j's only reference to com.nimbusds (oauth2-oidc-sdk, which itself depends on nimbus-jose-jwt) is declared with test scope in msal4j's own POM — a test-scope dependency does not propagate to a downstream consumer's compile/runtime classpath. Resolving the dependency tree for io.netty and com.nimbusds artifacts across every module that pulls azure-identity or msal4j transitively (the Azure extension, and the Databricks and MongoDB commercial extensions, which carry defensive ProGuard keep/dontwarn rules referencing com.nimbusds left over from an earlier dependency configuration) confirms zero resolved com.nimbusds:nimbus-jose-jwt artifacts anywhere in this repository's build. The scanner's finding does not correspond to an actual dependency in this codebase.

Netty HTTP/2 CONTINUATION frame validation bypass in codec. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious HTTP/2 frames to a Netty HTTP/2 server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP/2 server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport.

Path traversal and potential RCE via regression in Tomcat Rewrite Valve URL normalization. Requires an HTTP request to a running Tomcat server with the Rewrite Valve configured. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never configures the Rewrite Valve, and never accepts HTTP requests.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous event-driven network application framework. In netty-codec-compression versions 4.1.124.Final and below, and netty-codec versions 4.2.4.Final and below, specially crafted input can cause BrotliDecoder and certain other decompression decoders to allocate a large number of reachable byte buffers, leading to denial of service. Fixed in 4.1.125.Final of netty-codec and 4.2.5.Final of netty-codec-compression.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in netty-codec 4.1.125.Final / netty-codec-compression 4.2.5.Final; this repository's current build already resolves netty-codec 4.1.136.Final via the Azure and Cassandra extensions' Netty dependency chains, past the fix line. Liquibase does not accept compressed HTTP payloads from untrusted clients, and a source review found no code referencing BrotliDecoder, BrotliEncoder, BrotliOptions, or io.netty.handler.codec.compression.Brotli — the vulnerable decompression path is not exercised, regardless of version.

Go stdlib vulnerability in the Docker base image. Liquibase is a Java application and does not execute Go code at runtime. The Go binary is part of Docker base image tooling and is not invoked by Liquibase.

statements.status_notes: Due to the design of the name constraint checking algorithm, the processing time of some inputs scale non-linearly with respect to the size of the certificate. This affects programs which validate arbitrary certificate chains.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/x509 name-constraint vulnerability. NVD fixes the 1.25 line in Go 1.25.3 and the 1.24 line in Go 1.24.9; the scanner reported go1.25.1 for this image. Liquibase Secure only installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (docker/Dockerfile:39-55), and the entrypoint only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5). Repo-wide source greps found no crypto/x509, SystemCertPool, or CertPool usage in application code, so the arbitrary certificate-chain path described by the advisory is not exercised.

statements.status_notes: Validating certificate chains which contain DSA public keys can cause programs to panic, due to a interface cast that assumes they implement the Equal method. This affects programs which validate arbitrary certificate chains.
statements.impact_statement: Validating certificate chains with DSA public keys is not a reachable input path for Liquibase Secure. NVD fixes this in Go 1.25.2, but the Docker image only installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (docker/Dockerfile:35-55) and the entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5). Upstream lpm uses a default http.Client for downloads with no custom RootCAs or PEM loading logic (/tmp/gh-aw/agent/lpm/internal/app/utils/Http.go:13-25), so the arbitrary certificate-chain path described by the advisory is not exercised here.

False positive due to classifier confusion. Trivy reads the JAR's internal pom.properties which reports version 13.2.1 (without the jre11 classifier), causing a false version comparison. The installed JAR is 13.2.1.jre11 which contains the fix. Microsoft's non-standard Maven versioning uses a classifier suffix instead of a standard version bump.

statements.status_notes: GNU ncurses up to 6.5-20250322 has a stack-based buffer overflow in postprocess_termcap (tinfo/parse_entry.c) due to improper bounds checking during termcap entry processing, allowing a local attacker to trigger the overflow via a crafted termcap file, leading to denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: A stack-based buffer overflow in ncurses' termcap entry parsing requires a local attacker able to supply a crafted termcap file or TERM/TERMINFO value processed by an interactive terminal session. The Liquibase Secure container runs the CLI non-interactively via its entrypoint, without accepting untrusted local termcap input; TERM is set by the container orchestration layer, not by an untrusted local actor. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships libncursesw6 6.4+20240113-1ubuntu2.2, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: The processing time for parsing some invalid inputs scales non-linearly with respect to the size of the input. This affects programs which parse untrusted PEM inputs.
statements.impact_statement: Untrusted PEM parsing is not a reachable input path for Liquibase Secure. NVD fixes this in Go 1.25.2, but the Docker image only installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (docker/Dockerfile:35-55) and the entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5). Upstream lpm uses a default http.Client for downloads with no PEM parsing or certificate-loader code (/tmp/gh-aw/agent/lpm/internal/app/utils/Http.go:13-25), so the invalid-PEM parsing path described by the advisory is not exercised here.

statements.status_notes: The Reader.ReadResponse function constructs a response string through repeated string concatenation of lines. When the number of lines in a response is large, this can cause excessive CPU consumption.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib Reader.ReadResponse CPU exhaustion vulnerability fixed in Go 1.24.8 and 1.25.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), download it from the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 release (docker/Dockerfile:49), and the corresponding upstream liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3 declares go 1.25.10, which includes the fix. GitHub code search for liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 found no direct ReadResponse, net/textproto, or net/http usage, so the vulnerable API is not directly reachable from lpm source.

statements.status_notes: The ParseAddress function constructs domain-literal address components through repeated string concatenation. When parsing large domain-literal components, this can cause excessive CPU consumption.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib ParseAddress CPU exhaustion vulnerability fixed in Go 1.24.8 and 1.25.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), download it from the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 release (docker/Dockerfile:49), and the corresponding upstream liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3 declares go 1.25.10, which includes the fix. GitHub code search for liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 found no direct ParseAddress or net/mail usage, so the vulnerable email parsing API is not reachable from lpm source.

statements.status_notes: Using libcurl to do a transfer to a specific HTTP origin with Digest authentication and then changing the origin to a different one for a second transfer while reusing the same handle causes libcurl to wrongly pass on the Authorization header field meant for the first origin to the second. This flaw does not affect the curl command-line tool.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw is in libcurl's handle-reuse behavior: reusing the same handle for Digest-authenticated transfers to two different origins can leak the first origin's Authorization header to the second. Per curl's own advisory, this does not affect the curl command-line tool at all — only applications that reuse a libcurl handle across origins. The container's build steps use wget, not curl, for downloads, and the runtime entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI — a source review found no invocation of curl anywhere in this repository's Docker build or runtime path. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships curl 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.13, newer than the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Socket versions before 2.041 for Perl have an out-of-bounds heap read. pack_ip_mreq_source() in Socket.xs validates argument lengths in the wrong order, so a source address shorter than 4 bytes is not rejected and the copy reads up to 3 bytes past the end of its buffer, leaking adjacent heap memory into the packed structure.
statements.impact_statement: An out-of-bounds heap read exists in Perl's Socket module (pack_ip_mreq_source() in Socket.xs) when an application calls it with a multicast source address shorter than 4 bytes. Liquibase never invokes Perl or any Perl module (see the CVE-2025-15649 assessment on this same subcomponent for the reachability evidence). statements.status_notes: Perl through version 5.43.9 has a regex overflow flaw. Liquibase never invokes Perl or any Perl module (see the CVE-2025-15649 assessment on this same subcomponent for the reachability evidence), so no Liquibase security control is implemented via a Perl regex. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. statements.impact_statement:
Remediated. This affected bcprov-jdk18on before 1.85; Liquibase Secure now ships org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.85 via the managed bouncycastle.version pin in the root pom.xml, so the vulnerable code is not present in the distribution. statements.status_notes: A flaw was found in the libblkid library of util-linux. During nested partition probing, the BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, and UnixWare partition probers cache a raw pointer to a parent partition entry in a dynamically allocated array; when subsequent partition additions reallocate the array, the pointer becomes stale, leading to a heap use-after-free read. An attacker who can present a crafted block device image can trigger this without user interaction, since libblkid is invoked automatically by udev/udisks as root on block-device hot-plug events.
statements.impact_statement: This use-after-free in libblkid's nested partition probing (BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, UnixWare probers) is triggered automatically by udev/udisks as root on a block-device hot-plug event, such as a USB insertion or a loop-mounted disk image — containers do not perform hot-plug block-device management, and a source review of the Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no invocation of udev, udisks, blkid, or any partition-probing tool; the stock container's entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships bsdutils 1:2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: A flaw was found in p11-kit. The RPC message attribute parsing functions form a mutually-recursive call chain with no recursion depth limit when processing nested CKA_WRAP_TEMPLATE, CKA_UNWRAP_TEMPLATE, and CKA_DERIVE_TEMPLATE attributes. An unauthenticated attacker with local access to the p11-kit RPC Unix domain socket can send a specially crafted request with deeply nested template attributes, causing stack exhaustion and crashing the p11-kit server process and its dependent services.
statements.impact_statement: The reported package is inherited from the container base image. Exploitation requires a running p11-kit RPC Unix domain socket and local access to that service. Liquibase Secure does not start p11-kit or any auxiliary daemon: the container entrypoint only execs the Liquibase CLI, and a source review of the Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no reference to p11-kit or pkcs11. Without a p11-kit RPC service/socket in the deployed container, the required runtime environment is absent.

urllib3 vulnerability. urllib3 is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its HTTP client functionality is never invoked at runtime. All Python packages are pre-installed at build time via Maven graalpy-maven-plugin; no HTTP requests are made via Python at runtime.

statements.status_notes: (*x509.Certificate).VerifyHostname previously called matchHostnames in a loop over all DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. This caused strings.Split(host, ".") to execute repeatedly on the same input hostname. With a large DNS SAN list, verification costs scaled quadratically based on the number of SAN entries multiplied by the hostname's label count. Because x509.Verify validates hostnames before building the certificate chain, this overhead occurred even for untrusted certificates.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/x509 VerifyHostname quadratic complexity vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.11 and 1.26.4. The scanner reported affected Go stdlib versions in the lpm helper bundled in published Liquibase Secure Docker images. The Secure Dockerfile installs lpm as an optional helper (docker/Dockerfile:35, docker/Dockerfile:49), but the Docker entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is explicitly configured (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4); otherwise it executes the Java Liquibase CLI directly (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119). A focused grep across the Docker runtime files found no direct VerifyHostname, Certificate.Verify, matchHostnames, HostnameError, or crypto/x509 usage. Defense in depth: current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.5 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 declares go 1.25.11 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix.

Nesting depth constraint bypass in Jackson Core 3.x UTF8DataInputJsonParser and ReaderBasedJsonParser. maxNestingDepth from StreamReadConstraints is not enforced, allowing a deeply nested JSON document to cause StackOverflowError. Liquibase is a CLI tool that only parses JSON from trusted, operator-controlled configuration files and changelog artifacts. It does not expose any JSON parsing endpoint to remote or untrusted input. As established in the prior assessment of GHSA-2m67-wjpj-xhg9, Liquibase does not rely on StreamReadConstraints as a security boundary.

TLS 1.3 cipher suite preference order not preserved in Tomcat's SSL connector configuration. Requires an active TLS connector performing cipher negotiation. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or binds a TLS connector. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; no TLS handshakes occur.

statements.status_notes: Apache Tomcat authentication bypass where OCSP validation soft-fails even when soft-fail is explicitly disabled, allowing revoked client certificates to authenticate.
statements.impact_statement: Authentication bypass due to CLIENT_CERT soft fail misconfiguration in Tomcat's OCSP validation. Requires an active HTTPS connector configured with CLIENT_CERT authentication and an OCSP responder. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that uses picocli for command-line parsing and never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No connector, no authenticator, no OCSP — the code is inert.

Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or initializes clustering. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; EncryptInterceptor is never instantiated.

Fix: DAT-22804 bumps Go to 1.25.9 in liquibase-package-manager, eliminating the vulnerability at the source.

statements.status_notes: When using LookupCNAME with the cgo DNS resolver, a very long CNAME response can trigger a double-free of C memory and a crash.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib LookupCNAME double-free in the cgo DNS resolver when processing a very long CNAME response. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it downloads Liquibase extension driver JARs from GitHub release assets via HTTP. lpm never calls LookupCNAME — standard HTTP hostname resolution uses LookupIPAddr/LookupHost, not the CNAME-specific API. Additionally, the vulnerability requires the cgo DNS resolver, which is not the default on Linux; the pure-Go DNS resolver is active in the eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble container.

statements.status_notes: When processing HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames, transport will enter an infinite loop of writing CONTINUATION frames if it receives a SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0.

Exploitation requires a server to send the malformed SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE=0 frame. lpm only connects to trusted GitHub release CDN endpoints (URLs and checksums fixed in docker/Dockerfile:35-55); no attacker- controlled server endpoint exists in lpm's execution path.

statements.status_notes: Enforce a recursion limit in Unmarshal to prevent stack exhaustion when parsing deeply-nested, recursive structures.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib recursion-limit issue in Unmarshal. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. The secure Docker image installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50) and the runtime entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5). The default Liquibase runtime path executes the Java CLI directly, so the Unmarshal path that would process attacker-controlled deeply nested data is not exercised. This assessment also covers the GO-2026-5972 alias.

statements.status_notes: Netty HttpObjectDecoder incorrectly terminates chunk header parsing at \r\n inside quoted strings in chunked transfer encoding extensions, enabling HTTP request smuggling.

Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections. There is no listening socket for an attacker to exploit.

statements.status_notes: On Unix systems, opening a file in an os.Root improperly follows symlinks to locations outside of the Root when the final path component of the path is a symbolic link and the path ends in /. For example, root.Open("symlink/") will open "symlink" even when "symlink" is a symbolic link pointing outside of the root.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib os.Root symlink-following vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.12, 1.26.5, and 1.27.0-rc.2. The scanner reported affected Go stdlib version v1.26.4 in the lpm helper bundled in published Liquibase Secure Docker images (docker/Dockerfile:35, docker/Dockerfile:49) — confirmed by extracting the released liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 binary and running `go version` on it, which reports go1.26.4, matching the scanner's reported installed version exactly. The vulnerable API, os.Root (and OpenRoot), is a defensive filesystem-sandboxing API added in Go 1.24; a source-level grep of the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 repository for os.Root, OpenRoot, and .Root( returned zero hits, so lpm does not use the vulnerable API at all. Defense in depth: the Secure Docker entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is explicitly configured (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4); the default runtime path executes the Java Liquibase CLI directly and never calls lpm (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119-121).

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-27142 fixed a vulnerability in which URLs were not correctly escaped inside of a <meta> tag's <content> attribute. If the URL content were to insert ASCII whitespaces around the '=' rune inside of the <content> attribute, the escaper would fail to similarly escape it, leading to XSS.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib html/template escaping vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 declares go 1.25.10 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix. statements.status_notes: ReverseProxy can forward queries containing parameters not visible to Rewrite functions. When used with a Rewrite function, or a Director function which parses query parameters, ReverseProxy sanitizes the forwarded request to remove query parameters which are not parsed by url.ParseQuery. ReverseProxy does not take ParseQuery's limit on the total number of query parameters (controlled by GODEBUG=urlmaxqueryparams=N) into account. This can permit ReverseProxy to forward a request containing a query parameter that is not visible to the Rewrite function. For example, the query "a1=x&a2=x&...&a10000=x&hidden=y" can forward the parameter "hidden=y" while hiding it from the proxy's Rewrite function.

statements.status_notes: pgjdbc is an open source postgresql JDBC Driver. statements.status_notes:
Issue summary: A specially crafted PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed message could trigger a use-after-free during PKCS#7 signature verification.
Impact summary: A use-after-free may result in process crashes, heap corruption, or potentially remote code execution.
When processing a PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed message, if the SignedData digestAlgorithms field is present as an empty ASN.1 SET, OpenSSL may incorrectly free a caller-owned BIO during PKCS7_verify(). A subsequent use of the BIO by the calling application results in a use-after-free condition.
In the common case this occurs when the application later calls BIO_free() on the BIO originally passed to PKCS7_verify(). Depending on allocator behavior and application-specific BIO usage patterns, this may result in a crash or other memory corruption. In some application contexts this may potentially be exploitable for remote code execution.

statements.status_notes: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. Prior to versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final, Netty's `DnsResolveContext` insufficiently validates the bailiwick of NS records, enabling DNS Cache Poisoning. An attacker controlling an authoritative name server for a subdomain can poison the cache for parent domains (like `.co.uk`). In `io.netty.resolver.dns.DnsResolveContext.AuthoritativeNameServerList#add` method accepts any NS record from the AUTHORITY section as long as the record's name is a suffix of the questionName. Subsequently, the `handleWithAdditional` method caches the associated A records from the ADDITIONAL section directly into the `authoritativeDnsServerCache` under the parent domain's key. This bypasses standard bailiwick rules, where a server authoritative for a subdomain should not be trusted to provide authoritative records for its parent. The poisoned cache is then used for all future resolutions under the parent domain's key. Versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final patch the issue.

statements.status_notes: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. Because the object now IS an X509ExtendedTrustManager, neither SunJSSE's internal AbstractTrustManagerWrapper nor Netty's own OpenSslX509TrustManagerWrapper will re-wrap it to add endpoint-identification. Consequently, even though Netty 4.2 sets endpointIdentificationAlgorithm="HTTPS" by default, a client built with `SslContextBuilder.forClient().trustManager(somePlainX509TrustManager)` performs no hostname verification at all. Versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final patch the issue.

Silently absorbing other control characters can be exploited for request-boundary confusion where a front-end component treats those bytes differently.

statements.status_notes: channelBinding=require connections can be silently downgraded from SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS with channel binding to plain SCRAM-SHA-256 without it. An attacker able to intercept the TLS connection could exploit this by presenting certificates with unsupported signature algorithms, causing the authentication mechanism to lose its man-in-the-middle protection.
statements.impact_statement: pgjdbc channel-binding downgrade: connections configured with channelBinding=require can be silently downgraded from SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS (with channel binding) to plain SCRAM-SHA-256 (without it) when the server presents a certificate with an unsupported signature algorithm, defeating the MITM protection channelBinding=require is meant to provide. Fixed in pgjdbc 42.7.12. channelBinding is a pgjdbc JDBC URL/connection property; a repo-wide grep (`grep -rn "channelBinding" --include="*.java" --include="*.properties" --include="*.yml" .`) confirms Liquibase's own code never sets it. However, the --url argument is a raw user-supplied JDBC URL passed straight through with no property filtering (DbUrlConnectionCommandStep.java:107-120: `url = commandScope.getArgumentValue(URL_ARG)` flows unmodified into createDatabaseObject()), so a deployment where the user has appended channelBinding=require to their own connection URL — a deliberate, security-conscious choice some users make — remains exposed to this downgrade until the resolved pgjdbc version is 42.7.12+. This is therefore not reachable in Liquibase's *default* configuration, but is reachable if a user opts into channelBinding=require. Independently, the current source already pins the fix by default: pom.xml:62 sets postgresql.version to 42.7.13, and dist/pom.xml:123 consumes that managed version — the scanner reported 42.7.11 on the published 5.2.0 image (built before this version bump).

statements.status_notes: jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. From 2.10.0 until 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4, jackson-databind's PolymorphicTypeValidator (PTV) is the primary safety mechanism guarding polymorphic deserialization. When polymorphic typing is enabled and a type identifier contains generic parameters (i.e. the type ID string contains <), DatabindContext._resolveAndValidateGeneric() validates only the raw container class name (the substring before <) against the configured PTV. If the container type is approved, the method parses the full canonical type string via TypeFactory.constructFromCanonical() and returns the fully parameterized type without ever validating the nested type arguments against the PTV. The nested type arguments are then resolved, instantiated, and populated as beans during deserialization. An attacker who controls the type ID can therefore place a denied class as a generic type parameter of an allowed container — for example java.util.ArrayList<com.evil.Gadget> when only java.util.ArrayList is allow-listed. The container passes the PTV check; com.evil.Gadget is loaded via Class.forName(name, true, loader), instantiated, and its properties are set from attacker-controlled JSON. This completely bypasses an explicitly configured PTV allow-list. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4.
statements.impact_statement: jackson-databind's PolymorphicTypeValidator generic type validation bypass is fixed in 2.21.4 for the 2.x line. The scanner reported com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind 2.21.2 in the distribution build artifacts; the root POM declares jackson.version at 2.22.1 (pom.xml:57). Regardless of the exact installed version, the vulnerable code path is not reachable from Liquibase code: focused greps across Java sources for PolymorphicTypeValidator, BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator, activateDefaultTyping, enableDefaultTyping, JsonTypeInfo, constructFromCanonical, allowIfSubType, allowIfSubTypeIsArray, DefaultTyping, and _resolveAndValidateGeneric returned zero hits.

statements.status_notes: jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. A PTV built with allowIfSubTypeIsArray() plus an explicit concrete-type allowlist therefore still permits EvilType[] even though EvilType is not allowlisted. When Jackson deserializes the elements and no per-element type IDs are present, it instantiates the component type directly with no further PTV check, bypassing the allowlist. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.

Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Liquibase Secure installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP in core/docker/Dockerfile:23, core/docker/Dockerfile:44, core/docker/Dockerfile:49 and only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set in core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5. statements.status_notes: A malicious GOPROXY was previously capable of forging up to two sumdb tiles that allow for a requested module to bypass the GOSUMDB check and persist attacker-controlled module content to a local Go module cache. This attack allows for a malicious GOPROXY to serve malicious module content that cannot be detected by evaluating the transparency log. All tiles are now correctly verified against their parents. In order to determine if you have been affected: rm -r go.sum go.work.sum vendor/ && go mod tidy
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib GOPROXY sumdb-tile forgery issue. NVD fixes the Go 1.25 line in 1.25.13 and the 1.26 line in 1.26.6. The scan reported installed versions go1.25.3 and go1.25.1 for the bundled lpm helper across the supplied image tags. Liquibase Secure installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP in core/docker/Dockerfile:23, core/docker/Dockerfile:44, core/docker/Dockerfile:49 and only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set in core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5. statements.status_notes: sqlparse is a non-validating SQL parser module for Python. Prior to 0.6.0, SQL_REGEX in sqlparse/keywords.py and the per-position loop in sqlparse/lexer.py repeatedly scan unmatched dollar-quoted literal and multiline-comment delimiters, causing quadratic CPU consumption through sqlparse.parse(), sqlparse.format(), and sqlparse.split(). This issue is fixed in version 0.6.0.
statements.impact_statement: sqlparse is pinned at 0.5.3 in tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:864. The surrounding build plugin comment states these Python packages are only needed at build time and are never used at runtime (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:893, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:895), and the runtime implementation only references sqlparse in explanatory comments about a possible Python lock hang (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/main/java/com/liquibase/executor/PythonScriptExecutor.java:77, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/main/java/com/liquibase/executor/PythonScriptExecutor.java:240). The only actual import is in a test fixture (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/test/resources/scripts/badScript.py:4). NVD and GitHub both describe this as a sqlparse DoS fixed in 0.6.0, but the vulnerable parser is not reachable from the Liquibase runtime.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, the newHandshakeResponse methods of WebSocketServerHandshaker07 and WebSocketServerHandshaker08 complete a WebSocket protocol upgrade based solely on the presence of a Sec-WebSocket-Version: 7 (or 8) header, without verifying the mandatory Connection: Upgrade and Upgrade: websocket headers, enabling HTTP request smuggling / protocol-confusion attacks through intermediaries that don't recognize the request as an Upgrade. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: WebSocketServerHandshaker07/08 are server-side handshake classes, and neither module ever runs a WebSocket server: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty each only make plain HTTPS client calls, never WebSocket connections. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, HttpContentEncoder maintains a per-channel acceptEncodingQueue that accumulates attacker-controlled data without a size limit; the queue is filled on the I/O thread for every inbound HTTP request and drained only when the application writes a non-1xx response, allowing an attacker to exploit HTTP/1.1 pipelining to exhaust resources. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: HttpContentEncoder encodes outbound responses on the server side of an HTTP exchange, a role neither module ever plays: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty each only make outbound client requests and decode inbound responses, never run an HTTP server. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, Netty's HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.x translation layer (Http2StreamFrameToHttpObjectCodec / InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapter) fails to deduplicate or validate Host headers when an HTTP/2 client supplies both the :authority pseudo-header and a literal host header in a single HEADERS frame, producing an HttpRequest with two differing Host headers that can be used to bypass request-routing logic. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE concerns the HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.x translation layer a front-end server or proxy uses (e.g. InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapter) to receive and translate inbound HTTP/2 requests — a server/proxy-side concept neither module ever exercises, both being pure outbound HTTP/2 clients: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty each only ever act as a direct HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 client, never a protocol-translating front end. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http2 also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. In versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final, Bzip2Decoder's run-length encoding (RLE) state machine can enter an infinite loop when processing a malformed bzip2 stream, permanently occupying the event-loop thread at 100% CPU and causing denial of service. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: See CVE-2026-59901 entry on netty-codec above — same root cause (Bzip2Decoder RLE infinite loop), mirrored here so scanners that flag netty-codec-compression (the module Bzip2Decoder lives in for Netty 4.2.x) receive the same not_affected statement. Liquibase dependency management includes Netty versions below the fixed 4.2.16.Final release (cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-extension/pom.xml:65, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-deps/pom.xml:50, commercial-databases/liquibase-commercial-bigquery/pom.xml:72). No Liquibase Netty consumer adds Bzip2Decoder/Bzip2Encoder to a pipeline.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. In versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final, Bzip2Decoder's run-length encoding (RLE) state machine can enter an infinite loop when processing a malformed bzip2 stream, permanently occupying the event-loop thread at 100% CPU and causing denial of service. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: netty-codec resolves below the 4.1.136.Final fix line for both modules assessed here (4.1.130.Final for liquibase-commercial-cassandra via cassandra-jdbc-wrapper -> java-driver-core, 4.1.135.Final for liquibase-azure via azure-core-http-netty). The vulnerable class, Bzip2Decoder, is never reachable in either: the Cassandra native protocol's compression negotiation supports only LZ4/Snappy and this extension doesn't configure compression at all, while Azure's Netty HTTP client never wires a Bzip2Decoder into any pipeline (Azure HTTP responses use gzip/deflate/br, and a class-listing search of the Azure SDK jars for Bzip-related symbols returns zero hits).

statements.status_notes: Apache HttpComponents Client, when using the classic (blocking) I/O model, fails to release the underlying connection back to the connection manager if the response contains an invalid or unsupported Content-Encoding header value. Repeated requests to a malicious or misbehaving server leak connections and eventually exhaust the connection pool, producing a denial of service. The async I/O model is not affected. Fixed in version 5.6.3.
statements.impact_statement: httpclient5 is already pinned to 5.6.4 (past the 5.6.3 fix), but that alone only holds until a future downgrade, so we also checked reachability of the classic (blocking) client this CVE affects. Two usages exist: a bundled PII-detection filter, which is unreachable - it requires a policy-loading path Liquibase's checks engine never invokes - and the AWS SDK's synchronous Secrets Manager client, which is real but only ever talks to AWS's own TLS-authenticated endpoint. Exploitation needs that server to repeatedly send malformed Content-Encoding responses, so a remote attacker can't trigger this without already controlling or intercepting trusted AWS traffic - the same precondition used for the related Netty HTTP/2 CVEs.

statements.status_notes: Improper Access Control, Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat leads to security constraint bypass if a constraint for a longer path is specified before a more restrictive constraint for a shorter sub-path. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58, 9.0.121, which fixes the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Security constraint bypass when a `<security-constraint>` for a longer path is declared before a more restrictive constraint for a shorter sub-path in web.xml. Requires an active Tomcat servlet container evaluating security constraints against deployed web.xml descriptors. Liquibase is a CLI tool that uses picocli for command-line parsing and never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No servlet container is started, so no security-constraint evaluation ever occurs.

statements.status_notes: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's DIGEST authenticator. If, before windowSize requests have been made, a client makes a DIGEST authenticated request with a nonceCount on the upper boundary of the replay window then that request is replayable once only while the associated nonceCount remains within the replay window. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58 or 9.0.121, which fix the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Authentication bypass by capture-replay in Tomcat's DIGEST authenticator: a nonceCount on the upper boundary of the replay window can be replayed once before it ages out. Requires an active Tomcat servlet container with DIGEST authentication configured and processing inbound authenticated requests. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No DIGEST authenticator is ever configured or invoked.

statements.status_notes: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's FORM authentication process allows the bypassing of a security constraint that limits user access to a resource via POST but not GET. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58 or 9.0.121, which fixes the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Incorrect Authorization in Tomcat's FORM authentication process allows bypassing a security constraint that limits a user to POST access on a resource (not GET). Requires an active Tomcat servlet container with FORM authentication and a POST-only security constraint configured. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No FORM authenticator or security constraint is ever configured.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, io.netty.handler.codec.dns.AbstractDnsRecord, io.netty.handler.codec.dns.DefaultDnsRecordDecoder.decodeRecord(), and io.netty.handler.codec.dns.DnsCodecUtil.decompressDomainName() failed to release retained or newly allocated ByteBuf objects when IDN.toASCII() or encodeDomainName() rejected a malformed domain name, allowing unauthenticated remote DNS packets to leak direct memory incrementally until denial of service. Fixed in 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: netty-resolver-dns:4.1.135.Final (below the 4.1.136.Final fix line) resolves for this module via reactor-netty-http:1.2.18 -> reactor-netty-core:1.2.18, and unlike the other Netty CVEs assessed here, is genuinely wired into every outbound connection by default via reactor-netty-core's NameResolverProvider — this is not a code-not-reachable case. The hostname resolved is always operator-supplied configuration, never derived from changelog content: Key Vault modifiers parse the vault host from a Liquibase configuration value, and Blob Storage access uses a separately configured storage-account property, so an attacker can't inject a resolution target purely via a malicious changelog. That only rules out attacker-chosen domains, though — it doesn't rule out this CVE's actual mechanism, a malformed DNS response to an otherwise-legitimate query. DNS isn't TLS-authenticated the way this module's HTTP/2 traffic is, so the "trusted endpoint" argument used for the HTTP/2 CVEs on this module doesn't transfer here. Exploitation requires network-level access to the deployment's DNS resolution path — an assumption about the deployment environment this codebase can't verify. No newer reactor-netty release exists yet with a fixed Netty.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final, io.netty.handler.ssl.SslClientHelloHandler#decode checks the wrong offset before reading the four-byte TLS handshake header, so a ClientHello whose handshake header spans records can cause an IndexOutOfBoundsException and invoke select(ctx, null). This selects the default SslContext instead of the SNI-specific context. In deployments where per-SNI clientAuth=REQUIRE is the sole mutual TLS gate, the default SslContext uses clientAuth=NONE or clientAuth=OPTIONAL, and no application-layer certificate verification exists, an unauthenticated remote attacker can bypass the protected route's mutual TLS requirement. This issue is fixed in versions 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final.
statements.impact_statement: SslClientHelloHandler#decode checks the wrong offset before reading the four-byte TLS handshake header, so a ClientHello whose handshake header spans records can throw IndexOutOfBoundsException and fall back to the default SslContext instead of the SNI-specific one. This only becomes an mTLS bypass in a deployment that (a) runs a Netty server accepting inbound TLS connections, (b) uses per-SNI SslContext selection as the sole mutual-TLS gate (clientAuth=REQUIRE on the SNI context, weaker on the default), and (c) has no application-layer certificate check. Liquibase never runs a Netty server: a grep across all Java sources for ServerBootstrap, NioServerSocketChannel, SniHandler, AbstractSniHandler, and SslClientHelloHandler returns zero hits: netty-handler is present only as a transitive dependency of outbound HTTP/TLS clients (Azure SDK's azure-core-http-netty, the AWS SDK, the Couchbase client, the Cassandra JDBC driver). The scanner found netty-handler below the fixed versions in five bundled jars (Docker Scan run https://github.com/liquibase/liquibase-pro/actions/runs/34365994421): liquibase-commercial-cassandra.jar 4.1.119.Final, liquibase-azure.jar 4.1.135.Final, liquibase-aws-extension.jar 4.1.136.Final, liquibase-commercial-couchbase.jar 4.2.16.Final, and liquibase-azure-deps.jar (unlabeled in the scan, same shaded copy as liquibase-azure.jar); none of them run a Netty server, so the version gap does not matter to this assessment.

statements.status_notes: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.85, Name Constraints bypass via trailing dot in rfc822Name and URI. This issue also affects Bouncy Castle for Java LTS before 2.73.12, and Bouncy Castle for Java FIPS (BC-FJA) before bc-fips 1.0.2.7 (1.0.X series), 2.0.2 (2.0.X series) and 2.1.3 (2.1.X series).
statements.impact_statement:
Remediated. This affected bcprov-jdk18on before 1.85; Liquibase Secure now ships org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.85 via the managed bouncycastle.version pin in the root pom.xml, so the vulnerable code is not present in the distribution. The prior code-not-reachable analysis is retained below for the versions that shipped 1.78.1. [TECHOPS-1130]
Bouncy Castle Name Constraints bypass via trailing dot in rfc822Name and URI affects bcprov-jdk18on before 1.85. Liquibase Secure distribution includes org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.78.1 (core/liquibase-dist/src/main/archive/licenses/commercial/README.txt:1141), which is in the affected range. However, grep for direct `import org.bouncycastle.` usage across Java sources returned zero hits, and focused greps for NameConstraints, rfc822Name, GeneralSubtree, and PKIXNameConstraintValidator also returned zero hits. The only Bouncy Castle usage in production code is Snowflake private-key loading through the shaded `net.snowflake.client.jdbc.internal.org.bouncycastle.*` namespace in pro/src/main/java/com/datical/liquibase/ext/util/SnowflakeProJdbcConnectionUtil.java:7, pro/src/main/java/com/datical/liquibase/ext/util/SnowflakeProJdbcConnectionUtil.java:55, pro/src/main/java/com/datical/liquibase/ext/util/SnowflakeProJdbcConnectionUtil.java:57, and pro/src/main/java/com/datical/liquibase/ext/util/SnowflakeProJdbcConnectionUtil.java:73, which does not exercise certificate name-constraint validation or the standalone bcprov-jdk18on classes reported by the scanner.

statements.status_notes: Jackson Core 3.x maxNestingDepth constraint bypass in multiple parser implementations, enabling DoS via StackOverflowError from deeply nested JSON input.
statements.impact_statement: Repo-wide searches found no source declaration for tools.jackson.core:jackson-core. The build only references com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-core 2.22.1 at pom.xml:57,150-151, community-extensions/liquibase-mongodb/pom.xml:48,90-92, and core/liquibase-dist/src/main/archive/licenses/commercial/README.txt:137. The scanner-reported 3.1.0 coordinate is not present in the codebase.

statements.status_notes: Memory leak in Netty's DNS codec when processing malicious DNS response packets containing invalid domain names. The record decoder fails to release allocated ByteBuf resources before the IDNA-validation exception is thrown, allowing incremental memory exhaustion through sustained malicious DNS responses.
statements.impact_statement: Netty's DNS record decoder fails to release allocated ByteBuf resources before throwing on domain names that violate IDNA rules, leaking memory per malformed record. Unlike the server-side Netty DNS codec findings above, this path is reached during Liquibase's own outbound DNS resolution, but only triggers when the DNS server answering that resolution (or an on-path attacker able to forge responses) returns malformed records. This requires a compromised or malicious DNS resolution path — an attacker already in a position to forge DNS responses to Liquibase's outbound queries could achieve more direct impact (e.g. redirecting database connections) than a gradual memory leak. No CVE has been assigned to this advisory at the time of assessment. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections.

statements.status_notes: Jackson Core's async parser can accumulate excessively long digit sequences (~20,000x amplification of the intended maxNumberLength limit) when input is fed in small chunks without a terminator, weakening DoS protection for applications that rely on maxNumberLength.
statements.impact_statement: Incomplete fix for a prior number-length constraint bypass: Jackson's async/non-blocking parser (NonBlockingJsonParser / ByteArrayFeeder) silently buffers digit characters up to maxStringLength instead of enforcing maxNumberLength when input arrives in small chunks without a terminator byte. Found in jackson-core 2.22.0 bundled into liquibase-aws-extension.jar and liquibase-azure.jar. Both extensions are outbound clients that call AWS/Azure APIs and parse the responses those services return over TLS; neither extension's own code invokes Jackson's non-blocking parser API, and neither exposes a network-facing endpoint that accepts attacker-controlled JSON. Exploiting this would require an attacker already able to forge or MITM AWS/Azure API responses, at which point far more direct attacks are already available.

crypto/x509 name-constraint quadratic behavior is not reachable in the Liquibase Secure container. The secure Docker image installs lpm from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:39) and the runtime entrypoint only uses lpm to add mysql when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4). A repo-wide search found no code path that parses attacker-controlled certificate chains or invokes the affected x509 name-constraint APIs at runtime.

encoding/pem quadratic parsing behavior is not reachable in the Liquibase Secure container. The secure Docker image installs lpm from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:39) and the runtime entrypoint only uses lpm to add mysql when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh: 4). A repo-wide search found no code path that parses untrusted PEM input at runtime.

Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.5 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and the upstream liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 go.mod declares go 1.25.11 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which is newer than the scanner-reported Go 1.25.1 and includes the fix. GitHub code search for liquibase/liquibase-package-manager found no crypto/x509 imports or references, so the vulnerable certificate-chain path is not exercised by lpm source.
